artists.biography:
Supergrass was an English alternative rock band from Oxford. The band consisted of brothers Gaz (guitar and lead vocals) and Rob Coombes (keyboards), Mick Quinn (bass and backing vocals) and Danny Goffey (drums and backing vocals).
Gaz Coombes, Mick Quinn and Danny Goffey formed Supergrass in 1993 in Oxford with Gaz's brother Rob Coombes officially joining the band in 2002. The band signed to Parlophone records in 1994 and produced I Should Coco (1995), the biggest selling début album for the label since the Beatles' Please Please Me. Their first album's fourth single Alright was a huge international hit that established the band's reputation. Since then the band have released five albums: In It for the Money (1997), Supergrass (1999), Life on Other Planets (2002), Road to Rouen (2005) and Diamond Hoo Ha (2008), as well as a decade-ending compilation called Supergrass is 10 (2004).

perplexity.description:
In It for the Money, released in 1997, is the second studio album by English rock band Supergrass, issued under the BMG and Echo labels. Musically, the album blends elements of alternative rock, Britpop, glam, punk, and power pop, showcasing a more mature and varied sound compared to their debut. The band entered the studio with only two songs written, composing most tracks during recording, which contributed to its spontaneous and dynamic character. The album features a mix of energetic guitar riffs, catchy melodies, and occasional darker tones, exemplified by the ominous synth intro on the title track.

This album marked a significant step in Supergrass's discography, following their successful debut I Should Coco (1995). In It for the Money reached number 2 on the UK Albums Chart, reflecting strong commercial success. Critically, it was highly acclaimed; NME ranked it as the 10th best album of 1997 and praised its fun and inventive qualities, while Q magazine readers later voted it among the greatest British albums ever. The album's reception solidified Supergrass's reputation as one of the standout bands of the Britpop era, noted for their energetic and eclectic approach to rock music.
